citations.narrative:
One adult male caribou died due to complications from not having access to water for greater than or equal to 2.5 days.
On Friday, Sept. 5, 2025, the adult male was separated into a pen without a water trough or other source of water. The
animal caregiver for the weekend failed to notice the lack of water despite marking off on the daily checklist that the water
was checked. The animal was found dead on Monday, Sept. 8, 2025 and it was discovered that the animal had not had
any access to water since being placed in the separate pen. Necropsy revealed no obvious signs of illness or injury and
the veterinarian ruled that the death was due to lack of water.
Eleven adult females were locked out from water for at least 21 hours on June 2, 2026 despite the checklist being marked
as water checked. One adult female became severely ill with ruminal and metabolic acidosis requiring intensive medical
treatment and has survived so far as the time of inspection.
Lack of access to water can cause distress, illness including sever ruminal/metabolic acidosis, or death in animals.
Water must be provided as often as necessary for the health and comfort of the animal.
Corrections in place at the time of inspection. To be corrected from this date 7/24/2026 forward.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representative.
